- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days post-spike.
- Overshoots in mid-to-late forecast horizon (days 10–25) often occur when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if sentiment remains flat.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts; if true outcome shows sharp reversal from high peaks, model should adjust downward by 3–5% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment history is uniformly zero (no market sentiment signal), model should not assume strong directional bias; use historical volatility as anchor for correction.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in first 3–5 days, model should reduce subsequent forecast by 2–4% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often lag true price movements by 2–4 days; adjust for delayed reaction to news events or policy changes.
